jobs.title: Deputy Director of Environmental Health (0932 Manager IV)–DPH–167383
jobs.description:
Company Description

The Department of Public Health prioritizes equitable and inclusive access to quality healthcare for its community and values the importance of diversity in its workforce. All employees at the Department of Public Health work to advance equity, inclusion, and diversity with a specific lens and focus on race, ethnicity, gender, sex, sexuality, disability, and immigration status.

This is a Position-Based Test conducted in accordance with CSC Rule 111A.
Learn more about the City’s hiring process here: https://careers.sf.gov/knowledge/process/

Application Opening: Friday, September 4, 2026
Application Deadline: Application filing will close on or after Friday, October 2, 2026.
Salary: $173,264 to $221,052 Annually (Range A)
Appointment Type: Permanent Civil Service
Recruitment ID: PBT-0932-167383
Work Arrangement: Onsite

Amended September 18, 2026 To Update Minimum Qualifications.

Becoming a City employee means being a part of a team that cares about making a difference. Your work will shape both the present and future of San Francisco. When you work for the City, you’re choosing a job with purpose.

The Mission of the San Francisco Department of Public Health (SFDPH) is to protect and promote the health of all San Franciscans. Fulfilling this mission requires employees working across our hospitals, clinics, programs, and offices to deliver services and support the communities we serve. Individuals interested in joining SFDPH should expect to work in person across these settings.

The San Francisco Health Network, Population Health, Behavioral Health Services, and Administration are the core divisions of SFDPH. The San Francisco Health Network is the City’s only complete system of care and has locations throughout the City, including Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center, Laguna Honda Hospital and Rehabilitation Center, and over 15 primary care health centers. The Population Health Division (PHD) provides core public health services for the City and County of San Francisco: health protection, health promotion, disease and injury prevention, and disaster preparedness and response. Behavioral Health Services operates in conjunction with SFHN and provides a range of mental health and substance use treatment services.

SFDPH is intentionally evolving toward a department-wide, performance-managed operating model, requiring senior leaders who can set direction, drive execution, and deliver results across a highly complex public health and healthcare environment.

The eligible list resulting from this recruitment may be utilized to fill future and current vacancies in this class at other locations within the DPH for the duration of the eligible list.

Job Description

Reporting directly to the Director of Environmental Health, the Deputy Director of Environmental Health (0932 Manager IV) is responsible for ensuring effective daily operations across the Environmental Health Branch, supporting strategic priorities, and managing regulatory programs that may include Food Safety, Hazardous Materials and Waste, Healthy Housing, Water Quality, Solid Waste, Medical Cannabis Dispensary, Massage and Body Art, Tobacco Sales and Smoking, Site Mitigation and Local Oversight Program, City Hazardous Waste, Cellular Transmitter Site, and Disaster Planning.

The Deputy Director works closely with branch managers, City partners, and community stakeholders to advance environmental health protection, regulatory compliance, public health standards, and service excellence. The Deputy Director supports the Director in building a unified vision, motivating staff, and ensuring programs meet San Francisco’s complex public health and environmental regulatory needs.

The Deputy Director of Environmental Health (0932 Manager IV) performs the following essential job functions:

Develops and implements branch wide policies, procedures, strategic initiatives, and operational priorities
Leads daily operations for major Environmental Health regulatory programs, ensuring compliance, consistent performance, and alignment with public health mandates
Supervises Environmental Health program managers by assigning work and projects, providing operational and policy guidance, and participating in long range program planning, policy development, and the implementation of new environmental health programs
Oversees enforcement actions and serves as the primary hearing officer for abatement conferences, resolving complex, sensitive, or high-profile cases
Ensures quality, consistency, and continuous improvement across all regulatory programs by developing, implementing, and monitoring standard operating procedures, and by supporting environmental health assessments, data driven program development, and analysis of emerging environmental health issues
Leads workforce planning, ensuring appropriate staffing levels, staff development, and effective resolution of personnel and labor relations issues
Supports or leads legislative, regulatory, and policy development in coordination with SFDPH leadership, the Office of Policy and Planning, the Board of Supervisors, and other City partners
Participates in branch budget planning and oversight, monitoring program expenditures and ensuring fees and revenues reflect cost of service requirements
Represents the Environmental Health Branch in coordination with local, state, and federal agencies; engages with community organizations and industry groups; and communicates environmental health information at public meetings, hearings, and media or press events
Produces briefings for SFDPH leadership and serves as Acting Director as needed

The Deputy Director of Environmental Health (0932 Manager IV) may perform other duties as assigned/required.

Qualifications

REQUIRED MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

License: Possession of a valid license as a California Registered Environmental Health Specialist (REHS) OR eligibility to be admitted to and pass the Registered Environmental Health Specialist (REHS) examination per regulations (see Health and Safety Code Section 106670) within twelve (12) months of hire*, AND
Experience: Seven (7) years of experience in an environmental health agency of which three (3) years must include supervising environmental health professionals.
Note: Prior to hire, the finalist must submit a letter from the California Department of Public Health confirming eligibility to take the REHS examination within 12 months of hire, inclusive of all required education, experience, and training requirements.

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted. 

One-year full-time employment is equivalent to 2,000 hours (2,000 hours of qualifying work experience is based on a 40-hour work week).

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS: 
The stated desirable qualifications may be considered at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring.

Experience in a leadership role for local California Environmental Health jurisdiction
Possession of a Master’s degree in Public Health, Health Science, Public Administration, or a related field
Experience managing budgets and developing local ordinances
Experience supervising a large number of staff
Possession of a California Driver’s License

Verification of Education and Experience:

Every application is reviewed to ensure that you meet the minimum qualifications as listed in the job ad. Review SF Careers Employment Applications for considerations taken when reviewing applications.

Applicants may be required to submit verification of qualifying education and experience at any point during the recruitment and selection process. If education or experience verification is required, information on how to verify education and experience requirements, including verifying foreign education credits or degree equivalency, can be found at https://careers.sf.gov/knowledge/experience-education/.

Note:
Falsifying one’s education, training, or work experience or attempted deception on the application may result in disqualification for this and future job opportunities with the City and County of San Francisco.

Additional Information

Selection Procedures

After application submission, candidates deemed qualified must complete all subsequent steps to advance in this selection process, which includes the following.

Training and Experience (T&E) Evaluation (Weight: 100%)

Candidates that meet the minimum qualifications will be invited to participate in a Training and Experience evaluation that is designed to measure the knowledge, skills, and abilities in job related areas which may include but not be limited to:

Knowledge of environmental health principles, regulations, technical issues, and the environmental health branch’s programs, services, regulatory functions, and operational requirements
Ability to interpret and apply complex environmental and public health laws and regulations
Ability to supervise, mentor, and provide guidance to managers and professional staff, including assigning work, supporting staff development, and addressing personnel and labor relations matters
Knowledge of citywide and departmental policies, procedures, and program structures that guide operational and administrative decision-making
Knowledge of branch budget processes, including financial planning, forecasting, resource allocation, cost of service analysis, and monitoring of expenditures
Ability to communicate complex environmental health concepts clearly and effectively to diverse audiences, including executive leadership, elected officials, partner agencies, community groups, and the media
Ability to develop, interpret, and implement policies, regulations, and strategic initiatives, including analyzing complex environmental health issues and providing high level recommendations to executive leadership

Candidates will be placed on the confidential eligible list in rank order according to their final score.

Additional selection processes may be conducted by the hiring department prior to making final hiring decisions.

Certification

The certification rule for the eligible list resulting from this examination will be the  Rule of the List
.

Eligible List/Score Report

A confidential eligible list of applicant names that have passed the civil service examination process will be created and used for certification purposes only. An examination score report will be established, so applicants can view the ranks, final scores and number of eligible candidates. Applicant information, including names of applicants on the eligible list, shall not be made public unless required by law. However, an eligible list shall be made available for public inspection, upon request, once the eligible list is exhausted or expired and referrals resolved. The eligible list/score report resulting from this civil service examination process is subject to change after adoption (e.g., as a result of appeals), as directed by the Human Resources Director or the Civil Service Commission.

The duration of the eligible list resulting from this examination process will be 6 months and may be extended with the approval of the Human Resources Director.

To find Departments which use this classification, please see the city’s Position Counts by Job Codes and Departments.

Terms of Announcement and Appeal Rights

Applicants must be guided solely by the provisions of this announcement, including requirements, time periods and other particulars, except when superseded by federal, state or local laws, rules or regulations. Clerical errors may be corrected by the posting the correction on the Department of Human Resources website at https://careers.sf.gov/.

jobs.title: Air Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
Position Description

Purpose

The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer is responsible for preparing and submitting air quality permit applications for Teichert Materials stationary and portable equipment operations across California and western Nevada. The primary focus of this role is permitting: compiling emissions data for reporting, quantifying source emissions, preparing Authority to Construct (ATC) and Permit to Operate (PTO) applications, and managing them through district review to issuance.

This role serves as the company's technical resource for New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT) and toxics evaluations, CARB portable equipment (PERP) registration, and coordination with local air districts, the Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), and Northern Nevada Public Health. The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer supports facility- and equipment-level compliance, tracks permit conditions and renewal deadlines, and drives regulatory readiness and risk mitigation across the Teichert Family of Companies.

Focus & Scope

Essential duties and responsibilities, i.e. those which are basic, necessary, and an integral part of the job, are indicated below:

Air Quality Permitting and Regulatory Analysis

Prepare, submit, and manage complete and technically defensible air quality permit applications for new, modified, relocated, stationary, and portable equipment and sources, including Authority to Construct (ATC), Permit to Operate (PTO), and applicable portable equipment registrations.
Quantify source-specific emissions, including NOx, SOx, CO, VOC, PM/PM10/PM2.5, and toxic air contaminants, using applicable regulatory methodologies, emission factors, and accepted calculation methods.
Evaluate projects, facilities, and equipment to determine applicable permitting requirements, including exemptions, New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT), offsets, air toxics requirements, and other federal, state, and local regulatory requirements.
Review draft permit conditions prior to ATC issuance, and negotiate practical, enforceable condition language with district permit engineers to minimize operational and compliance burden while meeting air quality standards.
Manage permit applications through agency review and issuance, including responding to completeness determinations, deficiency notices, and technical inquiries; evaluating proposed permit conditions; and working with regulatory agencies to establish practical and enforceable permit requirements.
Coordinate air quality permitting with California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review and other regulatory processes when applicable.

Regulatory Compliance and Reporting

Maintain and administer air quality permits, registrations, compliance obligations, and regulatory deadlines for Company operations, including permit and registration renewals, monitoring, recordkeeping, emissions inventories, testing, and reporting requirements.
Prepare and submit required air quality regulatory reports and inventories, including applicable criteria pollutant and toxic air contaminant reporting, CARB Criteria and Toxics Reporting (CTR), greenhouse gas reporting, and AB 2588 Air Toxics “Hot Spots” reporting.
Administer applicable AB 2588 requirements, including toxic air contaminant emissions inventories, prioritization and risk screening, and coordination of required health risk assessments, public notifications, or risk-reduction activities.
Coordinate and oversee source (stack) testing for stationary equipment — scheduling required tests with certified testing firms, preparing and submitting source test protocols for district approval, coordinating district witnessing, and reviewing test reports for compliance with permit conditions and applicable emission limits.
Monitor facility and equipment compliance with applicable permit conditions and regulatory requirements, including fuel usage, throughput, hours of operation, emission limits, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting obligations; identify compliance risks and coordinate appropriate corrective actions.

Technical Evaluation and Field Support

Regularly access and evaluate active materials facilities, plants, equipment areas, and project sites to conduct source evaluations, obtain equipment and operational information, observe operating conditions, and support permitting and compliance activities (approximately 30% of work time, with the remaining time performing office-based permitting, analysis, and reporting functions). Site conditions may include uneven terrain, stairs or elevated areas, heavy moving equipment, dust, noise, and outdoor weather conditions.
Conduct or coordinate on-site evaluations of Company facilities, equipment, and project sites to identify applicable air quality permitting and compliance requirements and obtain technical and operational information necessary to support regulatory determinations, applications, and reporting.
Coordinate required source testing and other compliance evaluations, including test planning, regulatory agency coordination, review of technical results, and identification and resolution of potential compliance issues.
Provide technical guidance to operations, equipment, environmental, and project teams regarding air quality permitting and compliance requirements so regulatory considerations can be addressed during project planning, equipment acquisition or relocation, installation, and ongoing operations.

Agency and Organizational Representation

Serve as a Company technical representative and liaison with local Air Pollution Control Districts and Air Quality Management Districts, the California Air Resources Board (CARB), Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), Northern Nevada Public Health (NNPH), consultants, testing firms, vendors, and other external parties regarding air quality permitting and compliance matters.
Support regulatory inspections, internal audits, enforcement matters, and corrective actions by evaluating compliance issues, assembling technical documentation, responding to regulatory inquiries, and developing or coordinating appropriate corrective action plans.
Represent the Company, as appropriate, in industry groups and regulatory proceedings; monitor emerging air quality laws and regulations; evaluate potential impacts to Company operations; and assist in developing comments or recommendations regarding proposed regulatory changes.

Compliance Systems and Risk Management

Develop and maintain accurate, organized, and audit-ready permitting and compliance records, calculation tools, application templates, tracking systems, procedures, and other documentation necessary to support regulatory compliance and continuity of operations.
Maintain expert and current knowledge of applicable federal, California, Nevada, and local air quality requirements and evaluate regulatory developments that may affect Company operations.
Provide management with timely information regarding pending permit applications, regulatory deadlines, deficiencies, emerging requirements, and compliance risks, including recommended actions, responsible parties, and appropriate timelines for resolution.
Develop and improve permitting, workflow, and compliance processes, tools, and documentation to promote consistency, regulatory readiness, operational efficiency, and sustainable compliance across Company operations.

Relationships, Qualifications & Requirements, And Competencies

Key Relationships

Reports To

Environmental Manager, Teichert Materials

Direct Reports

N/A

External Clients

Public agencies, federal, state, and local regulatory agencies, subcontractors, vendors, general public

Internal Clients

President of Teichert Materials; Director of Aggregate Resource Development (ARD) and Environmental Compliance; Teichert Materials Plant Managers, Superintendents, and Administrative Staff; Teichert Services Group; ARD; Data and Technology Services (DTS); and other business units

Education

Bachelor's degree in environmental engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental science, or a related technical field preferred; equivalent combination of training, education, and experience will be considered.

Experience and Industry Expertise

Minimum of five (5) to eight (8) years of experience preparing air quality permit applications (Authority to Construct / Permit to Operate) for stationary or portable sources in California; experience with a California air district or as a permitting consultant preferred.
Working knowledge of the California local air district permitting system, New Source Review, BACT, air toxics evaluation, and CARB programs including PERP.
Experience with western Nevada air permitting (NDEP Bureau of Air Pollution Control and/or Northern Nevada Public Health) a plus.
Experience in the construction, aggregates, ready-mix, asphalt, or heavy equipment industries a plus.

Specific Job Requirements

Demonstrated ability to quantify source emissions using accepted emission factors and calculation methods, and to prepare complete, defensible permit applications.
Working understanding of how CEQA review interacts with air district permitting timelines.
Working knowledge of California AB 2588 (Air Toxics “Hot Spots”) requirements, including toxic emissions inventory, prioritization, and health risk assessment triggers.
Ability to interpret and apply federal, state, and local air quality regulations and to translate permit conditions into practical compliance requirements for field staff.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy; self-motivated with strong follow-through on applications and deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to negotiate permit conditions with district engineers and to explain requirements to non-technical staff in plain language.
Strong organizational and time-management skills; able to manage multiple concurrent applications and shifting district review timelines.
Strong project management skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel for emissions calculations, and the ability to quickly learn permitting and database tools.
Collaborative team player able to thrive in a matrixed management structure across multiple operating groups.
Commitment to workplace safety and support of corporate safety initiatives.
Willingness to adhere to the Company Code of Conduct consistently.
Some travel required to job sites and district offices in California and western Nevada.
Ability to travel regularly to Company facilities, project sites, regulatory agency offices, and other business locations throughout California and western Nevada.
A valid driver's license and acceptable driving record are required when operating a motor vehicle on Company business.
May require occasional work outside standard business hours, including early mornings, evenings, or weekends, to support regulatory deadlines, site activities, meetings, training, or time-sensitive operational matters.

Desirable Qualifications

Understanding of the working relationship between the CARB Portable Equipment Registration Program (PERP) and the Diesel Off-Road Online Reporting System (DOORS), including how portable and off-road diesel equipment is registered, reported, and kept compliant at both stationary facilities and temporary project sites.
Familiarity with distinguishing when equipment at a job site should be permitted by the local district, registered under PERP, or reported through DOORS, and how those pathways interact as equipment moves between sites.
Professional certification or coursework in air quality, environmental engineering, or a related field (e.g., QEP, CPEA, or equivalent).

Competencies

Building Relationships
Listening
Planning/Prioritizing
Initiative
Dependability
Judgement/Decision Making
Learning/Development
Managerial Courage
Safety

Equipment Used, Physical Demands, and Work Environment

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Specialist
jobs.description:
About the Role
Pinnacle Recruitment Services is seeking an experienced Environmental Compliance Specialist
to support our client's environmental compliance programs across multiple operational sites throughout California.
This is a contract-to-hire opportunity
with the intention of transitioning the successful candidate into a long-term position with our client.

This position is specifically focused on environmental compliance rather than occupational safety
. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with environmental regulations, permitting, inspections, regulatory reporting, and compliance programs within an industrial, energy, construction, consulting, or similarly regulated environment.

The ability to work independently is especially important
in this role. This individual will be responsible for managing assigned compliance activities, conducting field inspections, tracking deadlines, identifying potential issues, and following through on corrective actions with limited direct supervision. We are looking for a self-starter who is comfortable taking ownership of their responsibilities while effectively communicating and collaborating with operations and other internal teams.

The position combines field-based compliance work with administrative and regulatory responsibilities. Candidates located in Kern County are strongly preferred
and should be comfortable traveling independently to various project and operational sites throughout California. Occasional overnight travel may be required.

Key Responsibilities
Independently conduct environmental compliance inspections and audits at operational and project sites.
Review and interpret environmental permits, regulatory requirements, and associated compliance obligations.
Support environmental programs related to air quality, hazardous materials, hazardous and universal waste, water quality, stormwater, and spill prevention.
Proactively identify potential compliance concerns and assist with developing and implementing corrective actions.
Take ownership of assigned compliance activities and ensure required tasks and deadlines are completed accurately and on time.
Prepare and maintain environmental compliance reports, records, permits, plans, and supporting documentation.
Assist with environmental permit applications, regulatory reports, and other required agency submissions.
Track regulatory requirements, reporting deadlines, inspections, and other compliance obligations.
Support hazardous materials inventories, waste management programs, and associated reporting requirements.
Maintain organized environmental compliance records and regulatory files.
Support environmental incident response, documentation, and reporting.
Develop, review, and maintain environmental procedures and compliance programs.
Provide environmental compliance guidance and training to field and operations personnel.
Coordinate with internal teams, consultants, contractors, and regulatory representatives as needed.

Qualifications
Recent professional experience in environmental compliance is required.

Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage priorities, and take ownership of compliance responsibilities with limited supervision.
Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Engineering, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent professional experience will also be considered.
Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Experience reviewing and interpreting environmental permits and regulatory requirements.
Experience conducting environmental compliance inspections or audits.
Familiarity with environmental compliance programs such as CERS, CUPA, hazardous materials/waste management, SPCC, stormwater, air quality, and/or water quality compliance
.
Experience preparing environmental reports, regulatory documentation, permit applications, or compliance plans.
Previous interaction with environmental regulatory agencies is highly preferred.
Strong judgment and problem-solving skills with the ability to recognize potential compliance concerns and determine appropriate next steps.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Highly organized and detail-oriented with the ability to manage multiple compliance requirements and deadlines.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and electronic recordkeeping systems.
Valid California driver's license and acceptable driving record.
QSP, HAZWOPER, or other environmental compliance certifications are a plus.

Travel & Field Requirements
Regular travel to project and operational sites throughout California will be required. Candidates located in Kern County are strongly preferred
and must be comfortable traveling independently to various locations.
The position includes independent field work in outdoor and industrial environments and may involve varying terrain and weather conditions. Occasional overnight travel may be required.
Position Details
This position will begin on a contract-to-hire basis
, with the goal of transitioning the successful candidate into a long-term position with our client.

Mid-Senior level

The Air Quality Specialist / Engineer supports facility- and equipment-level compliance, tracks permit conditions and renewal deadlines, and drives regulatory readiness and risk mitigation across the Teichert Family of Companies.

Focus & Scope

Essential duties and responsibilities, i.e. those which are basic, necessary, and an integral part of the job, are indicated below:

Air Quality Permitting and Regulatory Analysis

Prepare, submit, and manage complete and technically defensible air quality permit applications for new, modified, relocated, stationary, and portable equipment and sources, including Authority to Construct (ATC), Permit to Operate (PTO), and applicable portable equipment registrations.
Quantify source-specific emissions, including NOx, SOx, CO, VOC, PM/PM10/PM2.5, and toxic air contaminants, using applicable regulatory methodologies, emission factors, and accepted calculation methods.
Evaluate projects, facilities, and equipment to determine applicable permitting requirements, including exemptions, New Source Review, Best Available Control Technology (BACT), offsets, air toxics requirements, and other federal, state, and local regulatory requirements.
Review draft permit conditions prior to ATC issuance, and negotiate practical, enforceable condition language with district permit engineers to minimize operational and compliance burden while meeting air quality standards.
Manage permit applications through agency review and issuance, including responding to completeness determinations, deficiency notices, and technical inquiries; evaluating proposed permit conditions; and working with regulatory agencies to establish practical and enforceable permit requirements.
Coordinate air quality permitting with California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review and other regulatory processes when applicable.

Regulatory Compliance and Reporting

Maintain and administer air quality permits, registrations, compliance obligations, and regulatory deadlines for Company operations, including permit and registration renewals, monitoring, recordkeeping, emissions inventories, testing, and reporting requirements.
Prepare and submit required air quality regulatory reports and inventories, including applicable criteria pollutant and toxic air contaminant reporting, CARB Criteria and Toxics Reporting (CTR), greenhouse gas reporting, and AB 2588 Air Toxics “Hot Spots” reporting.
Administer applicable AB 2588 requirements, including toxic air contaminant emissions inventories, prioritization and risk screening, and coordination of required health risk assessments, public notifications, or risk-reduction activities.
Coordinate and oversee source (stack) testing for stationary equipment — scheduling required tests with certified testing firms, preparing and submitting source test protocols for district approval, coordinating district witnessing, and reviewing test reports for compliance with permit conditions and applicable emission limits.
Monitor facility and equipment compliance with applicable permit conditions and regulatory requirements, including fuel usage, throughput, hours of operation, emission limits, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting obligations; identify compliance risks and coordinate appropriate corrective actions.

Technical Evaluation and Field Support

Regularly access and evaluate active materials facilities, plants, equipment areas, and project sites to conduct source evaluations, obtain equipment and operational information, observe operating conditions, and support permitting and compliance activities (approximately 30% of work time, with the remaining time performing office-based permitting, analysis, and reporting functions). Site conditions may include uneven terrain, stairs or elevated areas, heavy moving equipment, dust, noise, and outdoor weather conditions.
Conduct or coordinate on-site evaluations of Company facilities, equipment, and project sites to identify applicable air quality permitting and compliance requirements and obtain technical and operational information necessary to support regulatory determinations, applications, and reporting.
Coordinate required source testing and other compliance evaluations, including test planning, regulatory agency coordination, review of technical results, and identification and resolution of potential compliance issues.
Provide technical guidance to operations, equipment, environmental, and project teams regarding air quality permitting and compliance requirements so regulatory considerations can be addressed during project planning, equipment acquisition or relocation, installation, and ongoing operations.

Agency and Organizational Representation

Serve as a Company technical representative and liaison with local Air Pollution Control Districts and Air Quality Management Districts, the California Air Resources Board (CARB), Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), Northern Nevada Public Health (NNPH), consultants, testing firms, vendors, and other external parties regarding air quality permitting and compliance matters.
Support regulatory inspections, internal audits, enforcement matters, and corrective actions by evaluating compliance issues, assembling technical documentation, responding to regulatory inquiries, and developing or coordinating appropriate corrective action plans.
Represent the Company, as appropriate, in industry groups and regulatory proceedings; monitor emerging air quality laws and regulations; evaluate potential impacts to Company operations; and assist in developing comments or recommendations regarding proposed regulatory changes.

Compliance Systems and Risk Management

Develop and maintain accurate, organized, and audit-ready permitting and compliance records, calculation tools, application templates, tracking systems, procedures, and other documentation necessary to support regulatory compliance and continuity of operations.
Maintain expert and current knowledge of applicable federal, California, Nevada, and local air quality requirements and evaluate regulatory developments that may affect Company operations.
Provide management with timely information regarding pending permit applications, regulatory deadlines, deficiencies, emerging requirements, and compliance risks, including recommended actions, responsible parties, and appropriate timelines for resolution.
Develop and improve permitting, workflow, and compliance processes, tools, and documentation to promote consistency, regulatory readiness, operational efficiency, and sustainable compliance across Company operations.

Relationships, Qualifications & Requirements, And Competencies

Key Relationships

Reports To

Environmental Manager, Teichert Materials

Direct Reports

N/A

External Clients

Public agencies, federal, state, and local regulatory agencies, subcontractors, vendors, general public

Internal Clients

President of Teichert Materials; Director of Aggregate Resource Development (ARD) and Environmental Compliance; Teichert Materials Plant Managers, Superintendents, and Administrative Staff; Teichert Services Group; ARD; Data and Technology Services (DTS); and other business units

Education

Bachelor's degree in environmental engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental science, or a related technical field preferred; equivalent combination of training, education, and experience will be considered.

Experience and Industry Expertise

Minimum of five (5) to eight (8) years of experience preparing air quality permit applications (Authority to Construct / Permit to Operate) for stationary or portable sources in California; experience with a California air district or as a permitting consultant preferred.
Working knowledge of the California local air district permitting system, New Source Review, BACT, air toxics evaluation, and CARB programs including PERP.
Experience with western Nevada air permitting (NDEP Bureau of Air Pollution Control and/or Northern Nevada Public Health) a plus.
Experience in the construction, aggregates, ready-mix, asphalt, or heavy equipment industries a plus.

Specific Job Requirements

Demonstrated ability to quantify source emissions using accepted emission factors and calculation methods, and to prepare complete, defensible permit applications.
Working understanding of how CEQA review interacts with air district permitting timelines.
Working knowledge of California AB 2588 (Air Toxics “Hot Spots”) requirements, including toxic emissions inventory, prioritization, and health risk assessment triggers.
Ability to interpret and apply federal, state, and local air quality regulations and to translate permit conditions into practical compliance requirements for field staff.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy; self-motivated with strong follow-through on applications and deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to negotiate permit conditions with district engineers and to explain requirements to non-technical staff in plain language.
Strong organizational and time-management skills; able to manage multiple concurrent applications and shifting district review timelines.
Strong project management skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel for emissions calculations, and the ability to quickly learn permitting and database tools.
Collaborative team player able to thrive in a matrixed management structure across multiple operating groups.
Commitment to workplace safety and support of corporate safety initiatives.
Willingness to adhere to the Company Code of Conduct consistently.
Some travel required to job sites and district offices in California and western Nevada.
Ability to travel regularly to Company facilities, project sites, regulatory agency offices, and other business locations throughout California and western Nevada.
A valid driver's license and acceptable driving record are required when operating a motor vehicle on Company business.
May require occasional work outside standard business hours, including early mornings, evenings, or weekends, to support regulatory deadlines, site activities, meetings, training, or time-sensitive operational matters.

Desirable Qualifications

Understanding of the working relationship between the CARB Portable Equipment Registration Program (PERP) and the Diesel Off-Road Online Reporting System (DOORS), including how portable and off-road diesel equipment is registered, reported, and kept compliant at both stationary facilities and temporary project sites.
Familiarity with distinguishing when equipment at a job site should be permitted by the local district, registered under PERP, or reported through DOORS, and how those pathways interact as equipment moves between sites.
Professional certification or coursework in air quality, environmental engineering, or a related field (e.g., QEP, CPEA, or equivalent).

Competencies

Building Relationships
Listening
Planning/Prioritizing
Initiative
Dependability
Judgement/Decision Making
Learning/Development
Managerial Courage
Safety

new_jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Specialist
new_jobs.description:
About the Role
Pinnacle Recruitment Services is seeking an experienced Environmental Compliance Specialist
to support our client's environmental compliance programs across multiple operational sites throughout California.
This is a contract-to-hire opportunity
with the intention of transitioning the successful candidate into a long-term position with our client.

This position is specifically focused on environmental compliance rather than occupational safety
. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with environmental regulations, permitting, inspections, regulatory reporting, and compliance programs within an industrial, energy, construction, consulting, or similarly regulated environment.

The ability to work independently is especially important
in this role. This individual will be responsible for managing assigned compliance activities, conducting field inspections, tracking deadlines, identifying potential issues, and following through on corrective actions with limited direct supervision. We are looking for a self-starter who is comfortable taking ownership of their responsibilities while effectively communicating and collaborating with operations and other internal teams.

The position combines field-based compliance work with administrative and regulatory responsibilities. Candidates located in Kern County are strongly preferred
and should be comfortable traveling independently to various project and operational sites throughout California. Occasional overnight travel may be required.

Key Responsibilities
Independently conduct environmental compliance inspections and audits at operational and project sites.
Review and interpret environmental permits, regulatory requirements, and associated compliance obligations.
Support environmental programs related to air quality, hazardous materials, hazardous and universal waste, water quality, stormwater, and spill prevention.
Proactively identify potential compliance concerns and assist with developing and implementing corrective actions.
Take ownership of assigned compliance activities and ensure required tasks and deadlines are completed accurately and on time.
Prepare and maintain environmental compliance reports, records, permits, plans, and supporting documentation.
Assist with environmental permit applications, regulatory reports, and other required agency submissions.
Track regulatory requirements, reporting deadlines, inspections, and other compliance obligations.
Support hazardous materials inventories, waste management programs, and associated reporting requirements.
Maintain organized environmental compliance records and regulatory files.
Support environmental incident response, documentation, and reporting.
Develop, review, and maintain environmental procedures and compliance programs.
Provide environmental compliance guidance and training to field and operations personnel.
Coordinate with internal teams, consultants, contractors, and regulatory representatives as needed.

Qualifications
Recent professional experience in environmental compliance is required.

Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage priorities, and take ownership of compliance responsibilities with limited supervision.
Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Engineering, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent professional experience will also be considered.
Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Experience reviewing and interpreting environmental permits and regulatory requirements.
Experience conducting environmental compliance inspections or audits.
Familiarity with environmental compliance programs such as CERS, CUPA, hazardous materials/waste management, SPCC, stormwater, air quality, and/or water quality compliance
.
Experience preparing environmental reports, regulatory documentation, permit applications, or compliance plans.
Previous interaction with environmental regulatory agencies is highly preferred.
Strong judgment and problem-solving skills with the ability to recognize potential compliance concerns and determine appropriate next steps.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Highly organized and detail-oriented with the ability to manage multiple compliance requirements and deadlines.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and electronic recordkeeping systems.
Valid California driver's license and acceptable driving record.
QSP, HAZWOPER, or other environmental compliance certifications are a plus.

Travel & Field Requirements
Regular travel to project and operational sites throughout California will be required. Candidates located in Kern County are strongly preferred
and must be comfortable traveling independently to various locations.
The position includes independent field work in outdoor and industrial environments and may involve varying terrain and weather conditions. Occasional overnight travel may be required.
Position Details
This position will begin on a contract-to-hire basis
, with the goal of transitioning the successful candidate into a long-term position with our client.
